title: Snake
lastAssistantText:
**Fix applied and verified.** Here's the summary:

### Bug
In `tick()`, the self-collision loop iterated over all segments including the tail (`snake[snake.length-1]`). When the snake wasn't eating, the tail would be popped that same tick, but the collision check ran *before* the pop — causing a false game-over when the head moved into the tail's just-vacated cell (a legal move in tight loops).

### Fix
Added `eating` detection before the collision check:
- **When eating food** → tail won't be popped → check all `snake.length` segments (tail must be checked)
- **When not eating** → tail will be popped → check only `snake.length - 1` segments (exclude tail)

### Verification
- ✅ JS syntax valid
- ✅ HTML structure complete
- ✅ Wall collision unchanged (head outside 0..GRID-1)
- ✅ Food spawning unchanged (avoids occupied cells)
- ✅ Scoring, level/speed, pause, restart, localStorage all preserved
- ✅ Edge case: single-segment snake (`collisionLimit = 0`, no false collisions)

feedback.message:
DEFECT (self-collision) - verify against the original brief ("wall and self collisions"):

In tick() the self-collision check loops over EVERY segment of the snake, including the tail segment (snake[snake.length-1]). This check runs BEFORE the head is unshifted and BEFORE the tail is popped. So when the snake is NOT eating and the head moves into the cell that the tail currently occupies (a cell that will be vacated this same tick because snake.pop() runs in the else branch), the game wrongly reports a self-collision and calls endGame().

Why it is a real defect: in normal snake movement the tail advances one cell every tick the snake does not grow. Moving the head into the tail's just-vacated cell is legal play, e.g. rotating clockwise/counterclockwise around a tight loop or spiral. The current code terminates the game on that legal move.

Evidence: faithful reproduction of the exact tick collision loop (see .scratch/repro_tail_collision.js) with a snake traversing a closed 2x2 loop:
  snake = [head(1,1), (1,0), (2,0), tail(2,1)]
  moving right -> head target (2,1) == tail current cell
  app's self-collision check returns true (endGame) even though the tail pops that tick, leaving a valid snake [(2,1),(1,1),(1,0),(2,0)].

Expected behavior: the head moving into the tail's current cell should NOT end the game when the tail is about to move away that tick (i.e. when the snake is not eating food). The collision check should exclude the tail segment that will be removed this tick (compare against snake[0..length-2]) OR run the check after accounting for the pop. Only a genuine body collision should end the game.

Do not change: wall collision (head outside 0..GRID-1), food spawning on occupied cells, scoring, level/speed difficulty, pause, restart, localStorage high score. These currently behave correctly and should be preserved.
